stories.headline: Brent holds near [$94] on Gulf fears
stories.summary: Brent crude traded at $93.75 a barrel on 26 November, after settling up 3.69% at $94.90 the day before. WTI slipped 0.41% to $83.34. Traders are weighing Middle East supply risks and Hormuz shipping security against an expected oil surplus. US crude stocks rose 1.1 million barrels, and OPEC+ meets on 29 November.

stories.headline: Projectile explodes near tanker off Dubai - [crew safe]
stories.summary: UKMTO received a report of an explosion caused by an unknown projectile near a tanker about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai on Thursday. The ship's master reported the blast. The tanker was not damaged and there was no environmental impact. UKMTO says all crew are safe and accounted for. The vessel was not named.

stories.headline: Iran claims [LNG carrier and tanker] hit mines
stories.summary: Iran's military claims an LNG carrier caught fire after contacting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz on 25 November. A later statement claimed an oil tanker also struck a mine and caught fire in a restricted zone. No vessels were named. These are Iranian claims only - not independently confirmed.

stories.headline: Houthis threaten Saudi ports - [Hodeidah struck]
stories.summary: The Houthis threatened Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports and told shipping firms to move their vessels out. The Saudi-led coalition then struck Hodeidah port in Yemen after posting an evacuation warning, saying it hit operational capabilities there. No damage to ships was reported. Houthi-linked media also reported strikes near Sanaa airport - not verified.

stories.headline: Iran blacklists [26 tugboats] in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority blacklisted 26 tugboats on 24 November for assisting ships on the southern route near Oman. The tugs fly flags including Panama, Singapore, the UAE, Liberia, Mali and Tuvalu. The list reportedly now holds 266 vessels. Iran also claims 10 tankers were struck last week - not confirmed.

stories.headline: Engine room flooding leaves [AAL Gibraltar] dead ship
stories.summary: The Cyprus-flagged heavy-lift cargo ship AAL Gibraltar was disabled by flooding in its engine room. The 160-metre, 2010-built vessel was declared a dead ship and towed by salvage tug SPM Arjun to Hambantota, Sri Lanka. Four port tugs moved it to a lay-up berth. No departure date is confirmed yet.

stories.headline: Cruise crewman hit by [stray bullet] in Marseille
stories.summary: A 29-year-old cruise ship crewmember was hit by a suspected stray 7.62 mm bullet while resting near the quay at a Marseille shipyard around midnight. The bullet lodged under the skin near his neck. His injury is not life-threatening and he is stable in hospital. Police are reviewing footage; no suspect found.

stories.headline: China sets [LNG carrier delivery record]
stories.summary: Hudong-Zhonghua delivered the LNG carrier Seri Miri Princess to Petronas at Changxing Island, Shanghai, seven months ahead of schedule. It is the yard's 12th large LNG carrier delivered in 2026, a new Chinese annual record. Separately, Nigeria LNG's Bonny Gas Transport ordered two more LNG carriers there, taking its Shanghai programme to five.

stories.headline: Neda returns to VLCCs with [Chinese order]
stories.summary: Greek owner Neda Maritime Agency has returned to VLCC newbuilding with one firm ship plus an option at China's New Times Shipbuilding. Shipbrokers link the Lykiardopoulos family-controlled company to a 303,000 dwt deal. The order was reported on 25 November; price and delivery dates were not disclosed.
